records.summary: On Friday 27 October 2017 President Joao Lourenco exonerated Valter Filipe as governor of the Banco Nacional de Angola, and named Jose de Lima Massano in his place, returning Massano to the post he had held until January 2015 and taking him from the chairmanship of the executive board of Banco Angolano de Investimentos. Filipe had been appointed in March 2016 by the previous president, Jose Eduardo dos Santos. A note from the President's Civil House says the exoneration was at Filipe's own request, and the page gives no other official reason. It records that the exit came eleven days after the President criticised the BNA in a speech on 16 October, and does not say the speech caused the departure. Both things are in the record because the source states both and connects neither: the act is a presidential exoneration, and the only reason on the page is the governor's own request.
records.source_title: PR exonera governador do Banco Nacional de Angola (Ver Angola, 27 October 2017)

records.summary: On 30 November 2023 the standing parliamentary committee for Planning, Budget and Finance Affairs questioned National Bank of Ethiopia governor Mamo Mihretu for nearly four hours. The committee's chair, Desalegn Wodaje, called for renewed efforts against the parallel currency market and said the bank should use every policy option open to it, including devaluing the birr: in his words, the central bank has to use all policy options including devaluation, if it is necessary to bridge the widening gap. The report is dated 2 December 2023. This is a parliamentary committee telling the central bank which policy to adopt, in public, rather than an inquiry into the bank's conduct.
records.source_title: MPs squeeze regulators over parallel market, bank policies (The Reporter Ethiopia, December 2023)

records.summary: In a communique that reached the state news agency ACP on Wednesday 23 September 2026, the Cour des comptes, Congo's audit court, announced an audit mission at the Central Bank of the Congo (BCC). The mission is to examine the bank's treasury operations for the 2025 financial year, 'dans le cadre du controle de l'execution de la loi de finances de l'exercice 2025'. The court's First President, Jimmy Munganga, instructed the bank's services to hand the auditors the documents they need. The communique gives no start or end date for the mission. ACP notes that parliament's review of the 2025 accounts-settlement bill and of the 2027 finance bill depends on the court filing its report with the budget authority first.
records.source_title: RDC : la Cour des comptes annonce une mission d'audit a la Banque centrale (ACP, 23 September 2026)

records.summary: At a hearing on Monday 8 June 2026, at which the Auditor General presented consolidated financial statements for 31 March 2023 and 2024, Lesotho's parliamentary Public Accounts Committee called for a forensic audit of the Central Bank of Lesotho to trace missing public money. The committee's chairperson, 'Machabana Lemphane-Letsie, said the bank must undergo a forensic audit and say who the money had been paid to. The figures the report gives do not agree with each other: its headline puts the gap at M3.9 billion, while the statements it describes show government cash of M5.91 billion at 31 March 2024 against M2.82 billion in the Consolidated Financial Statements, a difference of M3.09 billion, and a quotation in the same piece also gives M3.09 billion. The committee resolved that the Auditor General's office submit a budget proposal for the forensic audit by 30 June so it could go into the supplementary budget; that office said it has neither the expertise nor any budget allocated for such an audit. The bank resisted, citing its own 2000 Act, which provides for an external auditor and limits the Auditor General to auditing currency balances rather than government payments the bank makes on the state's behalf.
records.source_title: PAC calls for forensic audit into missing M3.9bn (The Reporter, Lesotho, 12 June 2026)

records.summary: On 24 March 2023 Driss Sentissi, president of the Mouvement Populaire's parliamentary group, wrote to the presidency of the parliamentary commission on finance and economic development asking that Abdellatif Jouahri, wali of Bank Al-Maghrib, be summoned before parliament to explain the rise in the key rate from 2.5 per cent to 3 per cent. The Mouvement Populaire is an opposition party. The report does not say whether the commission agreed to summon him, so what is documented is the demand and not a parliamentary decision, and the record should be read that way.
records.source_title: Relevement du taux directeur: le MP reclame des explications d'Abdellatif Jouahri devant le Parlement (Le360, 24 March 2023)

records.summary: Central Banking reported on 30 July 2004 that President Maaouiya Ould Taya had sacked the chairman of the Central Bank of Mauritania, the day after sacking his whole economic team. The report names neither the sacked chairman nor any reason, and gives no calendar date, saying only that it happened on the Monday; the piece it relays, by IRIN, appeared on Wednesday 28 July. Zeine Ould Zeidane, formerly an adviser to the president, was installed in his place. The whole record rests on that one relayed report, so it is a claim, not confirmed.
records.source_title: Report says Mauritania's central bank chief sacked (Central Banking, 30 July 2004)

notes:
Round 53, moves-against-the-bank row, Africa block. Pre-checked all 14 target ISO3s against corruption.json, writeups.json and work/research_log_2026-11.json, and also against events_gold.json (which holds the moves layer): none of the 14 has a moves record. FILED 6: AGO, ETH, COD, LSO, MAR, MRT.

AGO: president's exoneration of governor Valter Filipe, 27 Oct 2017, from Ver Angola quoting the Casa Civil note to Lusa. The writeup already carries his 2020 conviction but not the dismissal, so this is new. Note the note says Filipe asked to leave; summary says so. A second AGO lead not opened: Ver Angola 9829, 'PR avisa banco central e critica distribuicao de divisas pelas mesmas empresas' (Oct 2017), which looks like a presidential public rebuke of the bank and would be a separate public-pressure record. Also unopened: lex.ao Decreto Presidencial 260/17 de 30 de Outubro, which may be the instrument itself (the press date and the decree date differ by three days).

ETH: parliamentary committee route worked. Planning, Budget and Finance Affairs standing committee took evidence from Governor Mamo Mihretu on 30 Nov 2023 and its chairman told the bank to use all policy options including devaluation. Not in the ETH writeup. Unopened further ETH leads of the same shape: ENA 'House Urges Central Bank to Maintain Tight Monetary Policy' (ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_6843068) and The Reporter 'Legislation looks to end central bank lending to government' (thereporterethiopia.com/40776/).

COD: Cour des comptes audit mission at the BCC, communique of 23 Sep 2026, from the state agency ACP. Distinct from the IGF 2021 BGFI finding and the 2023 account freeze already in the COD writeup. A second COD page was opened and REFUSED: actualite.cd, 14 June 2025, the Assemblee nationale ECOFIN commission (chair Guy Mafuta) heard Governor Marie-France Kabedi Malangu Mbuyi behind closed doors on 12 June 2025 on a bill amending the 2022 credit-institutions law. The bank is a witness on a bill about commercial banks, not the adversary of the state, so it does not qualify.

LSO: PAC demanded a forensic audit of the Central Bank of Lesotho over a 3.9bn maloti gap in government cash balances, June 2026. Dated only to the month because the source says 'Monday this week' without a calendar date. A companion LSO page was opened (lena.gov.ls, 'PAC grills CBL deputy governor on fraudulent transactions', Deputy Governor Lehlomela Mohapi, 2.6m maloti duplicate payments to MRP Enterprises flagged by the Auditor General); it carries a 2 July dateline with NO YEAR, so it is summarised inside the filed record rather than filed as its own dated episode. Worth a later round: the year of that sitting, and the Auditor General of Lesotho's own report.

MAR: filed the 24 Mar 2023 letter from Mouvement Populaire group head Driss Sentissi to the finance committee demanding the wali explain the rate rise. Honest caveat in the summary: a parliamentary group's demand, not a committee decision. REFUSED for MAR: fnh.ma 'Jouahri agace la classe politique' (pure characterisation) and medias24's 24 Nov 2020 live page on Jouahri's routine appearance before the Chamber of Representatives finance committee (an annual appearance, no state act against the bank).

MRT: filed the July 2004 sacking of the central bank chairman by President Maaouiya Ould Taya, dated to the month only, with the source's own limits stated in the summary (the man is unnamed, no reason given, Central Banking relaying IRIN). weak_source left false because Central Banking is a trade publication, not a blog, but the record says 'claim, not confirmed'.

NOT FILED, with reasons:
SWZ: a full qualifying episode exists but is ALREADY IN writeups.json - the Farmers Bank licensing fight, where Governor Majozi Sithole said a royal command required him to attend a meeting on 14 July 2017, finance minister Martin Dlamini told the bank in May 2018 that King Mswati III had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license the venture, a conditional licence followed in September 2018 after a royal command, and a 2022 Kroll forensic report commissioned by the bank said outside parties had likely instructed it to proceed. Per the brief I did not file it as new. If the layer should carry it, it can be lifted straight out of the SWZ writeup with no new research.
BWA: Bank of Botswana Amendment Act 2022 checked via Mmegi's feature on it - about 40 clauses, passed unopposed, described as adding protection from influence and tightening lending to government. That INCREASES autonomy, so excluded. Businessweekly headline 'Serame insulates MPC from political interference' points the same way. No parliamentary or Auditor General action against the bank found; the P100bn theft claim and the DPP's dismissal of it are already in the writeup.
SYC: fetched the Central Bank of Seychelles (Amendment) Act 2024 (Act 10 of 2024, passed 31 July 2024, assented 9 Aug 2024). It adds an express independence clause in s.3, and replaces presidential removal with a judicial tribunal under s.7A, so on balance it increases autonomy and is excluded. It also creates new routes for lending to government (s.40A force-majeure advances, s.40B credit from SDR proceeds), which a later round may want to weigh. Unopened SYC leads of the right shape: nation.sc 'FPAC hearings' (article 30563) and the National Assembly verbatim record of 25 June 2025.
RWA: opened The New Times, 18 Nov 2024, 'Central bank governor Rwangombwa explains lending rate decisions to parliamentarians'. The page names no committee, records no question or demand from MPs, does not say he was summoned, and the text is truncated, so there is no dated act by a named organ. Discarded. Untried for RWA: the allAfrica copy of the same story (allafrica.com/stories/202411190061.html) and the Office of the Auditor General's annual reports at oag.gov.rw, which earlier rounds also flagged as untried.
NAM: one search on the government-directive and law-change shapes returned only the Bank of Namibia Act 1 of 2020 (which replaced the 1997 Act) and routine Bank of Namibia briefings of a parliamentary standing committee, which the bank itself publicises as engagement, not an inquiry. Nothing filed. Untried lead worth a round: the Sovereign Wealth Fund Bill 2022 (civic264.org.na copy) and whether it moves the Welwitschia Fund out of the bank, plus Calle Schlettwein's 2019 tabling statement on the Bank of Namibia Bill at parliament.na.
COM: one French search on dismissal, inquiry, audit court and the 2025 statutes returned only BCC press releases, IMF documents and unrelated Comoros stories; the strongest Comoros-specific result was the Algeria governor revocation, a different country. Nothing filed. The standing arrangement that France names two of six board members, two of four on the banking supervision committee and two of four on the monetary policy committee under the statutes in force since March 2025 is already described in the COM writeup; it is the right shape for a standing-arrangement record with no end date if the main session wants it lifted across.
CPV: one Portuguese search on dismissal, parliamentary inquiry and audit returned only Boletim Oficial bulletin PDFs and Portuguese and Sao Tomean stories. Nothing naming a state act against the Banco de Cabo Verde. Untried: the Tribunal de Contas of Cabo Verde and the Assembleia Nacional's own records.
DJI: not searched this round; budget ran out after the six filings. Earlier rounds record Djibouti as repeatedly unreachable on other layers. Untried: the Cour des comptes of Djibouti and the Assemblee nationale record.
TZA and GMB skipped as instructed.
